title: Asset generation
author: gago8D
selftext:
What are some of the better tools people are using for generating assets for games?

Lately I’ve mostly been using ChatGPT for asset generation and honestly, I’ve been pretty impressed with how solid some of the results come out. But I’m wondering what other developers are using and if there’s a general consensus on what tools are actually worth learning/using.

Mostly looking for things like characters, environments, props, textures, etc. I’m open to anything — free or paid. Just curious what everyone’s go-to tools are right now.

comments.author: Quantizeverything
comments.body: For 3d assets I have had great luck with TripoAI + Astra. You can give Astra a skill that will use Tripo's API to generate models and will even place them into the game (im using godot). I can say "use tripo to model a tree and place it here" with a screenshot of my scene and it'll just do it.

replies.author: gago8D
replies.body: That’s pretty much what I do with ChatGPT. I’ll take a screenshot of a section of the screen and I’ll draw a circle where I want a fix or an asset placed.  And how’s godot?  I downloaded it yesterday I was thinking it might be good for my card game I’m making.

replies.author: Quantizeverything
replies.body: Its working so far but I need more time with the engine to decide if I actually like it.

comments.author: DepartmentPlus5191
comments.body: Depending on the art style, I usually try the same prompt in both ChatGPT Image and Gemini Nano Banana and then go with whichever fits better. If I need any extra elements, I sometimes use other generative AI tools from Alibaba Cloud as well.

replies.author: gago8D
replies.body: I’ve never heard of Gemini nano banana i has a funny name though I’ll have to give it a shot!

replies.author: DepartmentPlus5191
replies.body: Haha, the name definitely stands out! It's Google's image model, and I think their last big update was around early this year. Even so, it's still really useful when I want to try out certain art styles, so it's worth giving it a shot!

replies.author: gago8D
replies.body: I just tried it and added a picture of the loading screen to my game and it enhanced it really well.  I could probably use both chat GPT and Gemini they could be very useful together

replies.author: DepartmentPlus5191
replies.body: Great! I'm glad it was helpful

comments.author: HallucinatedGames
comments.body: I have game pipeline that runs locally. I use Stable Diffusion for Text to Images, Trellis 2 for Images to 3D GLB, and Stable Audio 3 Small for SFX. Services I use are Claude Code as my agent harness / driver. I use Google Lyra to generate music. I have used ChatGPT for some images I really want high quality on if needed.

replies.author: CauseQueasy8023
replies.body: Whats your vram? I tried the same setup a bit but results are horrendous

replies.author: HallucinatedGames
replies.body: I have an 8GB VRAM. Horrendus is a relative term LOL! :) But yes, I'm not going to win any game awards or probably art awards, especially with my limited VRAM and running the lower precision quants. These are hobby games I build (mostly with my kids as a family activity) and we use this pipeline to build stuff they come up with and then build gams we can play together. So your quality will vary based on many factors including your rig, what your goal is (professional versus hobby etc). All the games on my site have used this pipeline for the most part to get a flavor if your curious - [Hallucinated Games | Free AI-Generated Browser Games - Play Now](https://www.hallucinatedgames.com/)

replies.author: HallucinatedGames
replies.body:
The short version: the models are the easy part. What makes it run unattended is a catalog file, a status machine, and a runner that treats every asset as disposable.



The setup



Two ComfyUI instances, both headless, both driven over the HTTP API — I never open the GUI during a run. Main one on :8188 (SDXL + the ComfyUI-Trellis2 nodes), a second worktree on :8189 for Stable Audio 3, sharing the same models folder via a junction. Everything is POST /prompt with a workflow dict I build in code, then poll /history/<id>. Hardware is a 4060 (8 GB) on a 16 GB box, so nothing runs concurrently — that's a hard rule, contention silently trashes outputs.



The catalog is the actual unlock



I don't ask Claude to "make assets." I ask it to write catalog/assets.json — right now 175 entries. Each one:



{ "id": "prop\_wood\_crate\_small\_01", "category": "village\_clutter",

  "promptTemplate": "PROP",

  "promptDetails": "Rough-hewn planks, iron nail heads, corner brackets. \~0.6m tall.",

  "batch": 1, "status": "pending",

  "game": { "scaleMeters": 0.6, "collision": "box", "breakable": true,

"health": 20, "spawnWeight": 10, "maxCluster": 4 },

  "placement": { "near": \["house","tavern"\], "avoid": \["stream"\] } }



The plan is data, not a chat message. Prompts get composed at runtime: a shared base\_prompt.txt (centered, complete object, no ground plane, neutral studio light — all the things Trellis needs) + a category template (PROP / TREE / BUILDING / MODULAR / TERRAIN / SWAMP / VOLCANIC…) + that asset's promptDetails + a shared negative. So I tune one file and 175 assets change.



The stages, each writing status back into the catalog:



pending → SDXL (juggernautXL\_v9, 1024², 30 steps, cfg 7, euler\_a) → image validation (sharp: 20–90% object coverage, centered, not touching any edge, alpha or uniform bg — fails here, it regenerates with a new seed, up to 4 tries) → rembg → Trellis 2 (TRELLIS.2-4B, low\_vram, sparse → shape → decode → hole fill → quad remesh → simplify to 100k → texture at 1024) → GLB validation (gltf-transform: mesh/tri/material counts, bbox) → normalize (Y-up, origin at bottom-center, scaled to real-world meters from a table) → optimize (Draco + WebP) → copy into the game folder.



\~8–10 min/asset. Texture size 1024, not 2048 — 2048 was 50+ min each on this card.



Why it survives 8 hours alone



batch\_runner.py runs one subprocess per asset, 20-minute timeout, and verifies the GLB actually exists on disk before calling it done. Two strikes and the id goes into skipped.json and it moves on. A CUDA OOM costs me one prop, not the night. Seeds are hashed from the asset id, so reruns are idempotent. One shell script starts ComfyUI, waits for /system\_stats to answer, and kicks off the batch — that's the whole "goodnight" command.



Curating in the morning



A validator loads every GLB in real three.js in headless Chrome and checks pixels were actually drawn — catches files that parse fine but render nothing. It emits a contact sheet PNG, so I eyeball 40 props in one image instead of clicking through folders. Current honest numbers: 104 of 175 through, 19 rejected passes sitting in glb\_rejected/. Thin stuff (moss curtains, willow, wicker) just does not survive image-to-3D — the fix was prompt-level: "build as a SOLID CLOSED MASS, no thin strands, no wisps, no open lattice."



On "builds the environment" — that's a separate step and it's the metadata doing the work, not the 3D model. Map generators read spawnWeight / maxCluster / placement.near|avoid and lay out the level. Then a playtest harness drives the real game in headless Chrome with a bot and screenshots it, so the agent can actually see what it built. I also run a retint pass, because Trellis output comes out muted next to hand-made assets — +22% saturation, slight warm shift, originals kept so re-running never compounds.



Audio is the same shape: Stable Audio 3 Small (separate sfx/music checkpoints), 8 steps, cfg 1, lcm/simple, then a post script that trims from the first transient, fades 3 ms in / 40 ms out, crossfades loops, normalizes to -1 dBFS, FLAC → game WAV.



And one practical thing: I have Claude Code set up with remote control, so I can ping it from my phone during the day, see how the batch is going, and unstick it if it stalls. That matters more than it sounds — an 8-hour unattended run that dies at hour two is a wasted day otherwise.

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey! Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. I’d probably break this down by asset type rather than look for one “best” tool.

For 3D specifically, Tripo is worth testing for characters, props, and environment assets, but I’d still think of it as part of a workflow rather than the whole pipeline. The biggest question is what you need after generation: clean topology, rigging, animation, engine-ready export, printability, etc.

If you’re already happy with ChatGPT for concept/reference generation, pairing that with image-to-3D can be a pretty fast way to prototype assets.

Curious what kind of game you’re making and which asset category is your biggest bottleneck right now?

comments.author: Nilo_Team
comments.body:
for characters / env / props without living in blender-

nilo.io is free in the browser (monthly bits)- gen the mesh, hit model settings + LOD to cut polys, export GLB/FBX. auto-rig is bipedal T-pose only so humanoid chars land cleaner. no blender required for the gen→export loop.

won't cover every texture workflow but it's a solid go-to for game-ready assets. LMK :)
